title.de: War, waren: I was, you were
title.sl: Bil sem: I was, you were
title.it: Ero, eri: I was, you were

goal.sl: Poveš, kje je kdo bil in kakšno je bilo (I was, you were, wasn't, weren't), vprašaš Were you …? s kratkimi odgovori ter rečeš there was, there were in kdaj se je kdo rodil.
goal.de: Du sagst, wo jemand war und wie es war (I was, you were, wasn't, weren't), fragst Were you …? mit kurzen Antworten und sagst there was, there were und wann jemand geboren ist.
goal.it: Dici dov'era qualcuno e com'era (I was, you were, wasn't, weren't), chiedi Were you …? con le risposte brevi, e dici there was, there were e quando è nato qualcuno.
goal.en: You can say where people were and how things were (I was, you were, wasn't, weren't), ask Were you …? with short answers, and say there was, there were and when someone was born.

say.sl: Preteklik od **be** ima dve obliki. Za **I**, **he**, **she** in **it** je **was** (sem bil, je bil): **I was at the inn.** (Bil{m:|f:a} sem v gostilni.) **Jack was on the fell.** (Jack je bil na hribu.) **It was cold.** (Bilo je mrzlo.)
say.de: Die Vergangenheit von **be** hat zwei Formen. Bei **I**, **he**, **she** und **it** heißt sie **was** (war): **I was at the inn.** (Ich war im Gasthaus.) **Jack was on the fell.** (Jack war am Berg.) **It was cold.** (Es war kalt.) Vorsicht: **was** ist hier nicht das deutsche *was*.
say.it: Il passato di **be** ha due forme. Con **I**, **he**, **she** e **it** è **was** (ero, era; sono stato): **I was at the inn.** (Ero alla locanda.) **Jack was on the fell.** (Jack era sul monte.) **It was cold.** (Faceva freddo.)
say.en: The past of **be** has two forms. With **I**, **he**, **she** and **it** it is **was**: **I was at the inn.** **Jack was on the fell.** **It was cold.**

examples.en: Jack was on the fell all day.
examples.sl: Jack je bil ves dan na hribu.
examples.de: Jack war den ganzen Tag am Berg.
examples.it: Jack è stato sul monte tutto il giorno.

say.sl: Za **you**, **we** in **they** je **were** (si bil, smo bili, so bili): **We were tired.** (Bili smo utrujeni.) **They were at the market.** (Bili so na tržnici.) **you were** je tudi za eno osebo: **You were late, Sam!** (Zamudil si, Sam!) Ljudje rečejo tudi *you was*; v pisanju je **you were**.
say.de: Bei **you**, **we** und **they** heißt es **were** (warst, waren, wart): **We were tired.** (Wir waren müde.) **They were at the market.** (Sie waren auf dem Markt.) **you were** auch für eine Person: **You were late, Sam!** (Du warst spät dran, Sam!) Manche sagen auch *you was*; geschrieben steht **you were**.
say.it: Con **you**, **we** e **they** è **were** (eri, eravamo, erano): **We were tired.** (Eravamo stanchi.) **They were at the market.** (Erano al mercato.) **you were** anche per una persona sola: **You were late, Sam!** (Eri in ritardo, Sam!) C'è chi dice anche *you was*; per iscritto si usa **you were**.
say.en: With **you**, **we** and **they** it is **were**: **We were tired.** **They were at the market.** **you were** for one person too: **You were late, Sam!** People also say *you was*; writing wants **you were**.

examples.en: We were tired after the walk.
examples.de: Nach der Wanderung waren wir müde.

say.sl: Za zanikanje dodaš **not**: **wasn't** (was not) in **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** (Ni bilo mrzlo.) **The sheep weren't in the field.** (Ovc ni bilo na polju.) **I wasn't at home.** (Nisem bil{m:|f:a} doma.)
say.de: Zum Verneinen kommt **not** dazu: **wasn't** (was not) und **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** (Es war nicht kalt.) **The sheep weren't in the field.** (Die Schafe waren nicht auf der Weide.) **I wasn't at home.** (Ich war nicht zu Hause.)
say.it: Per dire di no aggiungi **not**: **wasn't** (was not) e **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** (Non faceva freddo.) **The sheep weren't in the field.** (Le pecore non erano nel campo.) **I wasn't at home.** (Non ero a casa.)
say.en: For no, add **not**: **wasn't** (was not) and **weren't** (were not): **It wasn't cold.** **The sheep weren't in the field.** **I wasn't at home.**

examples.en: The sheep weren't in the field this morning.
examples.sl: Ovc danes zjutraj ni bilo na polju.
examples.de: Die Schafe waren heute Morgen nicht auf der Weide.
examples.it: Stamattina le pecore non erano nel campo.

examples.de: Mr Dixon war nicht in der Schmiede.
examples.it: Il signor Dixon non era nella fucina.

say.sl: Za vprašanje gre **was** ali **were** na začetek: **Was it cold?** (Je bilo mrzlo?) **Were you at the show?** (Si bil{m:|f:a} na sejmu?) Kratki odgovor ponovi was ali were: **Yes, I was.** (Ja, sem.) **No, they weren't.** (Ne, niso bili.) Na severu rečejo tudi *Yes, I were*; v pisanju je **Yes, I was.** Nikoli *Yes, I wasn't*.
say.de: In der Frage kommt **was** oder **were** nach vorn: **Was it cold?** (War es kalt?) **Were you at the show?** (Warst du bei der Schau?) Die Kurzantwort wiederholt was oder were: **Yes, I was.** (Ja.) **No, they weren't.** (Nein.) Im Norden sagt man auch *Yes, I were*; geschrieben steht **Yes, I was.** Nie *Yes, I wasn't*.
say.it: Per chiedere, **was** o **were** va all'inizio: **Was it cold?** (Faceva freddo?) **Were you at the show?** (Eri alla fiera?) La risposta breve ripete was o were: **Yes, I was.** (Sì.) **No, they weren't.** (No.) Nel Nord dicono anche *Yes, I were*; per iscritto si usa **Yes, I was.** Mai *Yes, I wasn't*.
say.en: To ask, **was** or **were** goes first: **Was it cold?** **Were you at the show?** The short answer says was or were again: **Yes, I was.** **No, they weren't.** In the North people also say *Yes, I were*; writing wants **Yes, I was.** Never *Yes, I wasn't*.

examples.en: Were you at the show? — Yes, I was.
examples.sl: Si bil{m:|f:a} na sejmu? — Ja, sem.
examples.de: Warst du bei der Schau? — Ja.

examples.sl: So bile ovce na hribu? — Ja, so bile.
examples.de: Waren die Schafe am Berg? — Ja.
examples.it: Le pecore erano sul monte? — Sì.

say.sl: Z **was** in **were** gre čas, ki je mimo: **yesterday** (včeraj), **two days ago** (pred dvema dnevoma). Tudi **last night** (sinoči), **last week** (prejšnji teden), **this morning** (danes zjutraj); **ago** stoji zadaj. Iz **there is** je **there was**, iz **there are** **there were**: **There were a lot of people.** (Bilo je veliko ljudi.) **There was a dance at the inn.** (V gostilni je bil ples.)
say.de: Zu **was** und **were** passen vergangene Zeiten: **yesterday**, **two days ago** (vor zwei Tagen). Auch **last night** (gestern Abend), **last week** (letzte Woche), **this morning** (heute Morgen); **ago** steht hinten. Aus **there is** wird **there was**, aus **there are** **there were**: **There were a lot of people.** (Es waren viele Leute da.) **There was a dance at the inn.** (Im Gasthaus war Tanz.)
say.it: Con **was** e **were** vanno i tempi passati: **yesterday**, **two days ago** (due giorni fa). Anche **last night** (ieri sera), **last week** (la settimana scorsa), **this morning** (stamattina). **there is** diventa **there was**, **there are** diventa **there were** (c'erano): **There were a lot of people.** (C'era tanta gente.) **There was a dance at the inn.** (C'era un ballo alla locanda.)
say.en: With **was** and **were** go times that are over: **yesterday**, **two days ago**. Also **last night**, **last week**, **this morning**. **there is** becomes **there was**, **there are** becomes **there were**: **There were a lot of people.** **There was a dance at the inn.**

examples.de: Gestern Abend war Tanz im Gasthaus.

say.sl: Pazi na **where** (kje) in **were** (be): **Where were you?** (Kje si bil{m:|f:a}?) Zvenita in se pišeta drugače. In **born** gre z **was** ali **were**: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** (Teta Edna se je rodila leta 1952.) **Jack was born on the farm.** (Jack se je rodil na kmetiji.) Nikoli *is born*.
say.de: Achtung: **where** heißt wo, nicht wer, und **were** ist be: **Where were you?** (Wo warst du?) Und **born** geht mit **was**, nicht mit is: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** (Tante Edna ist 1952 geboren.) **Jack was born on the farm.** Nie *is born*, auch wenn man *ist geboren* sagt.
say.it: Attenzione a **where** (dove) e **were** (be): **Where were you?** (Dov'eri?) Si scrivono e suonano in modo diverso. E **born** va con **was** o **were**, dove l'italiano dice *è nato*: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** (Zia Edna è nata nel 1952.) **Jack was born on the farm.** Mai *is born*.
say.en: Watch **where** (a place) and **were** (be): **Where were you?** And **born** goes with **was**: **Auntie Edna was born in 1952.** (never *Auntie Edna is born in 1952.*) **Jack was born on the farm.**

translation.sl: Včeraj je bil v Keswicku tržni dan. Gospod Tyson je bil tam s svojim ovsom, babica Maggie in teta Edna pa tudi. Avtobus je bil zelo poln! — Si bil na tržnici, Jack? — Ne, nisem bil. Bil sem na hribu z Meg. Ovce v dežju niso bile vesele.
translation.de: Gestern war Markttag in Keswick. Mr Tyson war mit seinem Hafer dort, und Oma Maggie und Tante Edna waren auch da. Der Bus war sehr voll! — Warst du auf dem Markt, Jack? — Nein, war ich nicht. Ich war mit Meg am Berg. Die Schafe waren im Regen nicht glücklich.
translation.it: Ieri era giorno di mercato a Keswick. Il signor Tyson era lì con la sua avena, e c'erano anche nonna Maggie e zia Edna. L'autobus era pienissimo! — Eri al mercato, Jack? — No. Ero sul monte con Meg. Le pecore non erano contente sotto la pioggia.
translation.en: Yesterday was market day in Keswick. Mr Tyson was there with his oats, and Granny Maggie and Auntie Edna were there too. The bus was very full! — Were you at the market, Jack? — No, I wasn't. I was on the fell with Meg. The sheep weren't happy in the rain.

exercises.text: Old Wilf ___ born in 1942, on a farm by the tarn. Two days ago he ___ at the inn with Bess. There ___ a lot of people there, and there ___ music. — ___ it a good evening, Wilf? — Aye, it ___!

translation.sl: Stari Wilf se je rodil leta 1942 na kmetiji ob gorskem jezercu. Pred dvema dnevoma je bil z Bess v gostilni. Tam je bilo veliko ljudi in igrala je glasba. — Je bil lep večer, Wilf? — Ja, bil je!
translation.de: Der alte Wilf ist 1942 auf einem Hof am Bergsee geboren. Vor zwei Tagen war er mit Bess im Gasthaus. Es waren viele Leute da, und es gab Musik. — War es ein schöner Abend, Wilf? — Ja, das war er!
translation.it: Il vecchio Wilf è nato nel 1942, in una fattoria vicino al laghetto di montagna. Due giorni fa era alla locanda con Bess. C'era tanta gente e c'era la musica. — È stata una bella serata, Wilf? — Eh sì, proprio!
translation.en: Old Wilf was born in 1942, on a farm by the tarn. Two days ago he was at the inn with Bess. There were a lot of people there, and there was music. — Was it a good evening, Wilf? — Aye, it was!
